title: Rafael and the Alibi
premise: When founder Edmund Voss's coffin turns up empty, night dispatcher Dominic Iversen realizes the empty grave matches a call log entry they personally erased twelve years ago. As the sheriff's investigation stalls, Dominic quietly works the old dispatch records, discovering that the killer is someone who once sat in the same dispatch chair and has been watching them all along. The killer frames Dominic's chosen family—the taxi drivers who took them in as a runaway—to force silence, and the statute of limitations ticks down. In the climax, Dominic uses the company's own radio protocol to bait the killer into confessing on an open channel, trading their last shred of anonymity for the truth, and the book ends with the family intact but Dominic finally seen, named, and no longer invisible.
about_author: Sebastian Marchetti is the pen name of a former small-town newsroom clerk who spent a decade reading police blotters and obituaries side by side. Their fiction is known for quiet protagonists, procedural precision, and towns that keep their secrets the way banks keep ledgers.

chapters.title: The Grave That Kept Its Fare
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Dominic Iversen. During a storm-delayed exhumation, Edmund Voss's coffin is found empty, and Dominic recognizes the date instantly—it's the night of a call they erased from the dispatch log twelve years ago. The emotional beat is cold dread masked as professional detachment.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We learn how Dominic arrived at Voss Taxi at seventeen, invisible and unclaimed, and how filing the town's secrets became survival. The sheriff requests the old logs, and Dominic must decide whether to hand over the doctored file. Beat: the comfort of routine curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Twelve Years, One Missing Minute
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic reconstructs the erased call from memory: a driver's voice, a location, and a silence that lasted ninety seconds. They discover the log's backup tape is missing from the archive—someone got there first. Beat: the vertigo of realizing they're not the only one who remembers.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Maren Voss, Edmund's estranged daughter, who demanded the exhumation after receiving an anonymous letter containing her father's cufflink. Her grief is sharp and suspicious, and she fixes on Dominic as either ally or suspect. Beat: two guarded people circling each other.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Someone transmits on the company's old dispatch channel using call signs retired a decade ago—call signs only former employees would know. The drivers joke about a ghost; Dominic doesn't laugh. Beat: the past developing a voice.

chapters.title: The Man Who Trained Me
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Flashback chapter: Dominic's mentor, dispatcher Aldous Reeve, taught them the filing system—and vanished the same month the call was erased. Dominic visits his shuttered house and finds it recently lived in. Beat: loyalty beginning to feel like a debt with interest.

chapters.title: Sheriff Okonkwo's Short List
chapters.summary: Sheriff Okonkwo's POV. The investigation stalls; the sheriff quietly compiles a list of everyone with dispatch access over the years, and Dominic's name sits at the top. A tense interview where Dominic lies by telling the truth selectively. Beat: the hunter and the hider sharing one table.

chapters.title: What the Drivers Know
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through Dominic's observations. The taxi drivers—the family that took Dominic in—each hold a fragment of that night: a fare to the quarry, a burned jacket, a hushed argument. None will speak. Beat: found family as a wall of silence, loving and suffocating.

chapters.title: Cufflinks and Cold Cases
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren shares the anonymous letter with Dominic; the handwriting matches entries in Aldous Reeve's old dispatch ledgers. Together they confirm Reeve is alive and near. Beat: reluctant partnership, the first time Dominic chooses to trust instead of hide.

chapters.title: The Quarry Road Fare
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic maps the erased call's route: a pickup outside Voss's estate, a destination at the quarry, and a return trip logged under a false name. The coffin was never meant to hold Edmund. Beat: the case file assembling itself in Dominic's head like muscle memory.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The prosecutor reveals the homicide charge expires in thirty days; only a fresh felony—obstruction, tampering—can keep the case alive. Pressure lands on the taxi company, and the drivers begin turning on each other. Beat: time becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: A Farewell to Aldous
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic finally reaches Reeve by phone. Reeve is warm, paternal, and chillingly well-informed about Dominic's life—every address, every habit. He warns them off with affection. Beat: the mentor revealed as the watcher; loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Evidence implicating driver Ray Calvo—the man who gave Dominic their first bed—appears in the old archive: a planted log page, a doctored tape. Dominic realizes Reeve will burn the family to keep his secret. Beat: rage, and the end of neutrality.

chapters.title: Ray's Confession of Sorts
chapters.summary: Ray's POV. Ray admits he drove the quarry fare that night but swears Edmund Voss was alive when he dropped him—walking into the tree line with another man. He stayed silent to protect his brother. Beat: the cost of loyalty made explicit, a mirror held to Dominic.

chapters.title: Two Sets of Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Forensics on the coffin lining show two handlers: Reeve and someone with small hands—Dominic, from the night they helped rebury the box. Okonkwo confronts Dominic off the record and gives them one chance to come clean. Beat: the trap closing from both sides.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Maren and Dominic's POV. Following quarry records, they find a collapsed sinkhole shaft and, at its edge, a rusted dispatch headset—Reeve's, engraved. Edmund Voss never left the quarry. Beat: grief and horror braided together; the mystery becomes a body.

chapters.title: Open Channel
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic devises the trap: reopen the retired dispatch channel and broadcast, in the old protocol only Reeve taught them, a fabricated log entry placing surviving evidence with the prosecutor. If Reeve comes for it, he comes on tape. Beat: the invisible dispatcher finally using invisibility as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Last Dispatch
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax. Reeve takes the bait, arriving at the archive at 3 a.m. Dominic confronts him over the open channel while Okonkwo listens; Reeve confesses the cover-up—the founder's death was an accident he buried, then a secret he killed to keep. He turns on Dominic; the drivers arrive, having heard everything. Beat: terror, then the family standing between Dominic and the gun.

chapters.title: What Dominic Erased
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, aftermath. In a recorded statement, Dominic admits their own role—the erased minute, the reburial—and accepts consequences. Okonkwo, moved by the trap they ran, charges Reeve with murder and Dominic with a misdemeanor. Beat: the price of truth paid in full, and survivable.

chapters.title: Maren's Eulogy
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At the reburial—this time with Edmund in the coffin—Maren publicly thanks the taxi company and names Dominic as the one who brought her father home. Dominic, who has never been named in public, stands exposed and unharmed. Beat: being seen as grace instead of danger.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Log
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Weeks later, Dominic returns to the dispatch desk, the radio quiet, the file drawer finally honest. Reeve's trial is pending; the drivers bicker over coffee; Maren brings the company new business. Beat: the ordinary restored, but Dominic no longer hiding inside it.

chapters.title: The Alibi
chapters.summary: Closing chapter, Dominic's POV. A new dispatcher trainee asks Dominic why the old logs have gaps. Dominic tells the truth—the whole truth—for the first time, then teaches the kid the filing system, with one rule added: nothing gets erased. Final beat: legacy chosen over secrecy; the found family endures.
